chapters.title: Anatomy of Sound
chapters.content:
The Voice of Andreas Vesalius (2025-2026)

"Anatomy of Sound" is a contemporary musical work composed by Mathias Coppens for HERMESensemble.

Lasting approximately forty-five minutes, the piece explores the human body through sound, structure, and perception, drawing inspiration from the legacy of Andreas Vesalius.

chapters.title: Andreas Vesalius: A Revolutionary Anatomist
chapters.content:
Andreas Vesalius (1514-1564) was a pioneering Renaissance anatomist who transformed the study of the human body.

At a time when human dissection was widely prohibited, he conducted direct anatomical investigations, challenging long-standing misconceptions.

His detailed drawings and publications laid the foundations for modern anatomy and continue to influence medical science today.

chapters.title: A Life in Service of Knowledge and Power
chapters.content:
Born in Brussels into a family of physicians and pharmacists serving the royal court, Vesalius followed a path deeply rooted in medical tradition.

His expertise led him to serve as a physician to Emperor Charles V and later to Philip II of Spain, placing him at the intersection of science, politics, and royal authority.

chapters.title: Structure of the Composition
chapters.content:
The composition is divided into seven parts, echoing the structure of Vesalius' seminal anatomical work.

Each section focuses on a different aspect of the human body, such as nerves, muscles, the heart, and blood, translating physical systems into musical form.

Together, these parts create a layered exploration of the body as both a biological and symbolic entity.

chapters.title: The Voice of Andreas
chapters.content:
Complementing the musical work is a film by Mireille Capelle, titled "The Voice of Andreas."

Conceived as a reflective and interpretative portrait, the film explores Vesalius as both a historical figure and a representation of humanity.

While grounded in research, the film takes on a very personal viewpoint, offering a nuanced and imaginative perspective on his life and legacy.
